subject: Temporary burst 'parachute' pricing and reconciliation
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@paygrid.com>
To: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Short emergency burst for onboarding spike

Hi Monica / Ben,

Quick note from PayGrid — our new feature release rolled into production this morning and we’re seeing a 6x short-lived increase in inference traffic tied to user previews. We expect the surge to last 36-48 hours.

Can Redwood temporarily raise our token quota / rate limit to avoid throttling? We know this will likely be over our monthly commitment; we’re prepared to reconcile for the overage but want a predictable path for pricing tonight so our dashboard doesn’t cut requests.

Key ask: immediate +30% burst quota for 48 hours starting now, with a simple reconciliation at month-end (we can share invoices). Also helpful: what's the minimum per-hour rate you would charge for the temporary uplift?

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Director, Platform Ops — PayGrid

Attachments: paygrid_invoices_May2027.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)
From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@paygrid.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Short emergency burst for onboarding spike

Hi Alicia — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the release. We can stand up a temporary uplift immediately.

Operational summary: we can open a +30% burst window for 48 hours and route PayGrid traffic to a higher-rate class to avoid throttling. For transparency we propose a \"burst parachute\" model: an agreed per-token uplift rate for the window, capped total tokens covered by the parachute, and a month-end true-up where actual usage is reconciled against the cap.

Proposed terms (quick starter so we can move fast):
- Window: 48 hours from 2027-06-20T09:30 PDT
- Capacity: +30% quota across current routes
- Pricing: $0.012 per 1k tokens above committed rate (temporary uplift rate)
- Cap: apply parachute up to 150% of your committed monthly tokens (to limit exposure)
- Reconciliation: we will generate a provisional invoice for uplift usage; final true-up on 2027-06-30 with supporting usage report.

I’ve looped in Camila for routing + prefix caching notes and Ben for the commercial confirmation. If that sounds ok, Ben — can you confirm approval to proceed with those uplift charges and we’ll flip the switch?

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: parachute_pricing_sheet.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)
From: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>, camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-06-20T09:48:00-07:00
Subject: internal: PayGrid emergency burst — need confirmation on temporary rate and cap

Team — quick internal so we can avoid a live outage for PayGrid. They want +30% for 48 hours; Alicia attached May invoices. 

My proposal (see parachute_pricing_sheet.xlsx): $0.012 / 1k tokens uplift, parachute cap at 150% of committed monthly tokens. We should keep the cap tight to bound risk; PayGrid is comfortable reconciling.

Camila — any concerns about KV caching / cold-start hotspots if we flip routing? Anything we should do before we enable?
Laura — can you sign off on the temporary price and confirm how we'll capture this in billing (provisional invoice + month-end true-up)? If approved, I’ll let them know and enable immediately.

Thanks — M

Thanks — I reviewed the attached sheet. Finance is OK to proceed with the parachute model provided we:
- Generate a provisional invoice immediately for estimated uplift (so PayGrid has predictable spend on their side)
- Run final reconciliation on 2027-06-30 with a detailed tokens-by-route export
- Limit internal write-off authority: anything > $25k needs VP finance approval (we don't expect to hit that given the cap)

Please collect a signed email acknowledgement from PayGrid agreeing to the uplift rate and cap; capture their billing contact for the provisional invoice. I will prepare the billing entry and a true-up template.

Laura Bennett
Director of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
